Entry final class

One row in a Pane's listing — a file, directory, or symlink found in the current directory. Immutable value object.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly string $name, public readonly bool $isDir, public readonly int $size, public readonly int $mtime, public readonly bool $isLink = false, public readonly bool $isHidden = false, public readonly string $linkTarget = '', public readonly bool $linkBroken = false, public readonly int $mode = 0, public readonly int $uid = -1, public readonly int $gid = -1)
static parent(): self
isParentSentinel(): bool
displaySize(): stringDisplay string for the size column. Links render the localized LINK token FIRST (CF-45, closes 081), directories the DIR one (CF-16, closes 056 — the tokens stood raw in all 16 locales before), regular files their byte size compacted to KB/MB/GB/TB (units stay language-neutral per the finding). The link check must precede the directory one because isDir deliberately FOLLOWS links (navigate() must be able to enter a link-to-dir) — checking isDir first made every symlinked directory answer DIR and hide its link nature from the row.
static humanSize(int|float $bytes): stringCompact byte count (B/KB/MB/GB/TB, language-neutral units). Shared by the size column and the CF-52 info overlay's size / free-space lines.
static symbolicMode(int $mode): stringCF-52: ls-style symbolic mode (drwxr-xr-x) from a raw st_mode, including setuid/setgid/sticky in the x slot the way ls prints them.
static sanitizeName(string $s): stringStrip every terminal-control construct so a filename is inert when rendered: complete escape sequences first (OSC strings consumed whole with their parameters, likewise CSI; other ESC-initiated ECMA-48 sequences lose only their introducer to the generic leg — a DCS string is not consumed up to its ST, so its parameter body stays behind), then a sweep of every leftover C0 control, ESC, and DEL byte, then C1 controls in BOTH spellings: the UTF-8-encoded form (\xc2\x80-\xc2\x9f) and lone 8-bit bytes (0x80-0x9F) outside a valid UTF-8 sequence, per the sugar-core Ansi/Sanitize doctrine — a raw \x9b acts as CSI for many terminals, so it must never reach one. Canonical multi-byte text is matched whole first and survives (日本語, é); a dangling lead byte of an invalid sequence degrades to printable junk, the same intentional outcome the ESC legs accept.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly string $cwd, array $entries, public readonly int $cursor = 0, array $selected = [], public readonly Sort $sort = Sort::NameAsc, public readonly bool $showHidden = false, public readonly bool $readable = true, public readonly bool $tooLarge = false)
static open(string $cwd, \Closure $lister, Sort $sort = Sort::NameAsc, bool $showHidden = false): selfBuild a fresh Pane for $cwd by listing entries via $lister and applying the current sort order.
navigate(\Closure $lister): selfMove into the directory under the cursor (or up if it's the .. sentinel). Files don't navigate — caller decides what to do with them (open in viewer, edit, etc.).
unreadable(): selfA copy of this pane carrying the same listing with the "cannot read" truth attached (CF-22). The preserved entries are the LAST HONEST READ, not a phantom: the directory simply stopped answering between reads.
tooLarge(): selfA copy of this pane carrying the same listing with the CF-13 "too many entries" truth attached: readable = false (the same refusal shape CF-22 established — the listing shown IS the last honest read) plus tooLarge, so callers name the cap instead of wrongly blaming permissions.
relist(\Closure $lister, ?bool $showHidden = null): selfRe-read this pane's directory IN PLACE, preserving the selection and cursor where they still make sense: a selected name survives only if the entry still exists, and the cursor stays on the entry it was on (falling back to a clamped index).
moveCursor(int $delta): self
withCursor(int $index): selfPark the cursor on an absolute entry index, clamped into the list (CF-55: a mouse click names a row, not a delta).

gotoBottom(): self

withSelected(array $wanted): selfReplace the selection with the given name→true map, keeping only names that are actually listed here right now (CF-31). The parent sentinel can never be marked — it is navigation furniture, not a file, and every operation walks real entries.

Callers must not ask while search / help / info / a confirm gate replaces the browse frame.

Sort enum

Sort orders for the pane listing. Directories always group at the top regardless of order; the comparator below applies the order as the secondary key.

Cases: NameAsc · NameDesc · MtimeAsc · MtimeDesc · SizeAsc · SizeDesc · ExtAsc · ExtDesc

PHP also provides cases(), from() and tryFrom().

MethodSummary
apply(array $entries): arraySort $entries in place (returns a new list — pure). .. parent sentinel stays at index 0 if present.
static extension(string $name): stringCF-46: the sort suffix of a file name — the run after the LAST dot, lower-cased so 'Photo.JPG' groups with 'notes.jpg'. A name with no dot, or whose only dot leads it (.bashrc — a dot-file is a NAME, not an extension), has the empty suffix and so groups at the front of an ascending run.
label(): stringCF-16 (closes 060): the localized field label the pane header shows in place of the raw enum notation ('name-asc' is a wire value, not user chrome). Every arm spells its literal key — tests/LangCoverageTest greps literals, so a built key would look used to the forward scan and unused to the reverse one.
isAscending(): boolDirection of the order; rendered as the language-neutral ↑/↓.
cycle(): selfCycle the active sort: every tap of s alternates the direction, and the field advances on the following tap — from NameAsc the order is NameDesc, MtimeAsc, MtimeDesc, SizeAsc, SizeDesc, ExtAsc, ExtDesc, back to NameAsc. e is the CF-46 direct selection of the extension field.

Version final class

The version string this tool reports on --version.

MethodSummary
static line(): stringThe --version line: plain text, newline-terminated, produced by no state and no host probe — the flag must answer anywhere.
static current(): stringThe version this process reports: the archive stamp when running from a stamped phar, self::CURRENT everywhere else.
static fromPharMetadata(string $path): ?stringThe version a phar archive at $path was built to carry, or null when it names none (unreadable archive, wrong metadata shape, the dev-build sentinel, or an empty stamp). Every refusal is a null, never an exception — --version must answer on a machine whose phar cannot be opened.
static versionFromMetadata(mixed $metadata): ?stringThe judgement on the stamp itself, split out because the archive-open leg is unreachable from a suite that must not build phars: the release namespace strip, the dev-build refusal, and the wrong-type nulls are a pure function over what getMetadata() answers.
static hostArchive(): stringThe filesystem path of the phar this process was launched from, or '' when it was not launched from one — the two-identity law measured on candy-code's real builds and pinned by the bin autoload guard: inside archive-loaded code Phar::running(false) answers the archive path, while the stub context answers '' and there a '.phar'-suffixed __DIR__ is the enclosing archive.
